Got a chance to talk to P_c about this skip, and a few articles they brought to my attention for potential wikiwalk links included SCP-427 and SCP-329. Both of these objects could have potentially catastrophic effects on human life if cross testing them with SCP-135 goes south, and it is likely the Foundation may just hedge their bets and keep them separated by a good distance. Recommending the addition of the following edits:

Changing this:

SCP-135 is to be contained in a partitioned plexiglass chamber at least 7 metres to a side. All sections are to be completely sealed off from one another to avoid cross-contamination. SCP-135 itself is to be in a central section with 1.0 to 1.5 square metres of floorspace, with a 5 cm-wide runoff trench around the perimeter that drains into a tank, the contents of which are to be piped into an incinerator at the end of every week. The remaining space in the containment chamber is to be used to house 5 chemical harvesting vats, one vat per partitioned section. A single access corridor is to lead from SCP-135's section to outside the chamber. No personnel are permitted within SCP-135's effect radius; all maintenance, taking of samples, etc., are to be carried out by remote-control robots. Disciplinary measures need not be taken against personnel that violate this rule, because the direct consequences of SCP-135's effects have been deemed consequence enough. Robots are to be maintained and cleaned by Level 1 personnel.

Once a week, SCP-135's section is to be hosed down with Solution U82-B until only its outer coating is visible. In emergencies, flamethrowers may be employed to reduce mass quickly.

To this:

SCP-135 is to be contained in a partitioned plexiglass chamber at least 7 metres to a side. All sections are to be completely sealed off from one another to avoid cross-contamination. SCP-135 itself is to be in a central section with 1.0 to 1.5 square metres of floorspace, with a 5 cm-wide runoff trench around the perimeter that drains into a tank, the contents of which are to be piped into an incinerator at the end of every week. The remaining space in the containment chamber is to be used to house 5 chemical harvesting vats, one vat per partitioned section. A single access corridor is to lead from SCP-135's section to outside the chamber. No personnel are permitted within SCP-135's effect radius; all maintenance, taking of samples, etc., are to be carried out by remote-control robots. Disciplinary measures need not be taken against personnel that violate this rule, because the direct consequences of SCP-135's effects have been deemed consequence enough. Robots are to be maintained and cleaned by Level 1 personnel.

Once a week, SCP-135's section is to be hosed down with Solution U82-B until only its outer coating is visible. In emergencies, flamethrowers may be employed to reduce mass quickly.

Due to the potential of catastrophic effects in the event of cross contamination, at no point are are SCP-329 or SCP-427 to be contained within the same facility.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: By the power of Necroposting, I have the Secret Backstory Details!
item.content:encoded:
Five years later, now that I've fully fleshed out SCP-135's exact origins…

SCP-135 feels what I noted in my original comment, but, additionally, is upset because she can't hear her father/"father" anymore, since the containment site isn't on the mountain. Don't get me wrong — she's fully locked-in and couldn't reply — but it's the difference between hearing a kind voice sometimes and not.

She's a wish-child, granted by one of the old gods of the hills to an otherwise infertile woman, but when she asked for "life, in the form of a child", he thought she meant "Life"-with-a-capital-L, and a mountain's idea of what it means to "survive adversity" is… not the same as a human's, to say the least. It turns out that the abstract concept of Life can't completely "fit" into a human body, but since the other parts of the wish prevent her from turning into, say, an SCP-427-style flesh beast, SCP-135 is instead conceptually leaky. All the excess "aliveness" violently crams itself into any other living cell it encounters, for lack of anywhere else to go, and in the process breaks everything holding that cell back from making more cells for it to be in.

item.title: Re: CANCER DOES NOT WORK THAT WAY! GOODNIGHT!
item.content:encoded: Yes, SCP-135 induces irreversible changes to gene regulation of cells. Being in the AoE additionally removes the need for a nutrient source and causes the cells to multiply at an unnaturally fast rate. When removed from the AoE, the affected cells are still cancerous, but they revert to acting like non-anomalous cancer cells.

item.title: CANCER DOES NOT WORK THAT WAY! GOODNIGHT!
item.content:encoded: So, speaking as a biologist, if you're giving people cancer as a result of exposure to this SCP then any cells you remove from the area of effect should likewise continue growing uncontrollably with a nutrient source. Meaning, this SCP must cause irreversible changes to gene regulation in the cells. The alternative is that cells only grow uncontrollably while in the AoE of this SCP, in which case the cancerous growths would revert to their previous characteristics upon removal from the SCP and all you'd have is a test subject with some really nasty-looking benign neoplasias or maybe a good teratoma or two.
